title: Two People Running for Georgia Governor Hold a TV Debate
summary:
This year, 36 states are choosing a governor. A governor is the leader of a state. In Georgia, the two main candidates met this week for their only debate on TV.

One candidate is Keisha Lance Bottoms, a Democrat who used to be the mayor of Atlanta. The other is Rick Jackson, a Republican businessman. Right now, Jackson is a little ahead in the polls.

Voters got to ask the candidates questions. They asked about the cost of living, cameras that read license plates, data centers, pay and a government health program called Medicaid.

Bottoms said Jackson has claimed he does not disagree with any of President Donald Trump's policies. Jackson did not say Trump's name. He compared himself to Georgia's current governor, Brian Kemp. Trump has endorsed Jackson.

Jackson's supporters said they like that he is a businessman and not a longtime politician. He is also spending lots of money on TV ads.

Today, the U.S. has 26 Republican governors and 24 Democratic governors.
why_it_matters: The governor helps make decisions about things kids use every day, like schools and roads.
